rendered:
The paper gives limonene and nerolidol titers in several places, and they do not fully agree.

Limonene: the terpenoid paragraph says that the Wang et al. platform reached 14.12 g L^(cid:0) 1[1] in shake flasks and bioreactors. Elsewhere the paper says that (S)-limonene reached 22.8 g L^(cid:0) 1[2] (highest reported), and the summary table lists (S)-limonene at 22,800[3] mg/L (fed-batch, citing the terpene-synthase engineering work). So the higher limonene value is consistent between the text and the table, but the lower value appears only in the terpenoid paragraph and is not carried into the table.

Nerolidol: the same terpenoid paragraph reports 32.33 g L^(cid:0) 1[4] in the same sentence. The introduction, the sesquiterpene text and the summary table all give (E)-nerolidol as 70.50 g L^(cid:0) 1[5] (table: 70,500[6] mg/L, fed-batch). So the higher nerolidol value is consistent across the introduction, the text and the table, while the lower value appears only in the terpenoid paragraph and is not in the table.

Summary: the higher limonene and nerolidol values agree across sections. The lower limonene and nerolidol values appear only in the terpenoid paragraph, are not reproduced in the summary table, and are not reconciled with the higher values. That paragraph also does not clearly say whether each value came from shake flasks or bioreactors. The discussion mentions limonene and nerolidol as platform products without giving titers.

expect: two different studies: the multicopy-integration platform gave limonene 14.12 g/L and nerolidol 32.33 g/L in 5-L bioreactors (p11.L1-2, ref [16]); later optimisations gave (S)-limonene 22.8 g/L (p11.L15, ref [21], Table 2 22,800) and (E)-nerolidol 70.50 g/L (p11.L20, ref [24], Table 2 70,500). Not a contradiction, different strains and studies.
